 Comm Min amends certain rules of Export Promotion Mission initiative to support exporters 
 The Commerce Ministry has modified guidelines to expand participation of exporters in international trade events. These changes include increased airfare reimbursements for exporters to encourage their participation in trade fairs. PTI

The Commerce Ministry has modified the guidelines on the ₹25,060 crore Export Promotion Mission to expand exporters' participation in international trade events, improve market access, and enhance support for MSMEs facing geographical disadvantages, an official statement said on Wednesday. To enable wider participation and provide enhanced support, the Department of Commerce has amended the Guidelines for Market Access Support , Trade Regulations, Accreditation and Compliance Enablement and Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport under the Niryat Disha Sub-Scheme. Under Market Access Support, the guidelines have been amended to increase the maximum export turnover level from ₹75 lakhs in the previous year to ₹50 crore to be eligible for availing reimbursement of airfare for participating in buyer-seller meets (BSMs), trade fairs, and trade delegations. The government will also enhance airfare reimbursement to up to 95 per cent for Micro and Small Exporters and up to 80 per cent for other eligible exporters. The Market Access Support intervention seeks to strengthen India's export market access through structured support for activities such as buyer-seller meets (BSMS), reverse buyer-seller meets (RBSMS), trade fairs, exhibitions, and related market access initiatives. Under the amended guidelines, the list of certificates eligible for reimbursement has been expanded from 462 to 600. It is aimed at enabling greater coverage of support to MSMEs to meet internationally recognised quality, safety, and technical requirements. The Trade Regulations, Accreditation and Compliance Enablement intervention seeks to provide support to MSMEs to meet internationally recognised quality, safety, and technical requirements arising from compliance and quality-related certificates. Similarly, under the Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT), the ministry has extended support to low export intensity districts in 34 states/UTs from the existing 13 states/UTs; and the category of ports to which transport is reimbursed was expanded to include Land Customs Station (LCS) and Integrated Check Post (ICP). The amended guidelines also added incentives for goods movement through waterways in addition to existing road, rail and air transport modes. Air freight support for export shipments has been extended to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, in addition to the existing coverage of the North Eastern Region. The Logistics Intervention for Freight and Transport seeks to address geographical disadvantages and logistics gaps affecting MSMEs in low export intensity areas by providing support to lower freight and logistics costs stemming from the locational challenges faced by MSMEs in these regions.
